Flexible instruments can create adequate femoral tunnel lengths at 90° of knee flexion in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. According to one study, using flexible instruments via an anteromedial portal allows for safe and effective femoral tunnel creation without excessive knee hyperflexion.

This is because the 90° flexion position enables optimal alignment of the femoral tunnel with the anatomical landmarks, reducing the risk of tunnel too short or too long. Additionally, studies have shown that flexible instruments can achieve satisfactory tunnel lengths even at this specific flexion angle.

Furthermore, another study found that medial and lateral posterior tibial slopes (PTS) were significantly steeper in failures of ACLR than the control group. This suggests that both medial and lateral PTS ≥ 5° may be associated with increased risk of ACLR failure. Therefore, using flexible instruments to minimize knee flexion can help mitigate this risk.

In summary, flexible instruments used correctly at a 90° of knee flexion position can create adequate femoral tunnel lengths in ACL reconstruction, reducing the risk of complications and improving outcomes for patients.
